speaker: Sheldon
text: I was analyzing our lie, and I believe we're in danger of Penny seeing through the ruse. Simple. If you were to log on to www.socalphysicsgroup.org/activities/other, click on upcoming events, scroll down to seminars, download the PDF schedule, and look for the seminar on molecular positronium, well then, bippity boppity boo, our pants are metaphorically on fire.

speaker: Leonard
text: What? How?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, sir, my trousers will not be igniting today. Penny! Penny! Penny! Good morning.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Of course I do. My watch is linked to the atomic clock in Boulder, Colorado. It's accurate to one tenth of a second. But as I'm saying this, it occurs to me that once again your question may have been rhetorical.

speaker: Penny
text: Do you have any idea what time it is? What do you want?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Remember how Leonard told you we couldn't come to your performance because we were attending a symposium on molecular positronium?

speaker: Penny
text: I remember symposium.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, well, he lied.

speaker: Penny
text: Wait, what?

speaker: Sheldon
text: He lied, and I'm feeling very uncomfortable about it.

speaker: Penny
text: Well, imagine how I'm feeling.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Hungry? Tired? I'm sorry, this really isn't my strong suit.

speaker: Leonard
text: You told her I lied? Why would you tell her I lied?

speaker: Sheldon
text: To help you.

speaker: Leonard
text: I'm sorry, I'm not seeing the help.

speaker: Sheldon
text: She was going to see through your lie eventually, so I told her that you were lying to protect me.

speaker: Leonard
text: Oh, I'm getting a bad feeling.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Hunger? Indigestion? I'm sorry, I'm really not very good at this. Anyway, Penny now believes that on Friday night, we're going to participate in my cousin Leopold's drug intervention.

speaker: Leonard
text: Your cousin Leopold?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Who most people call Leo, but he also answers to Lee. Remember that, it's important.

speaker: Leonard
text: What's important?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Details, Leonard. The success or failure of our deceitful enterprise turns on details.

speaker: Leonard
text: Do you have a cousin Leopold?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, I made him up. I think you'd call him Lee.

speaker: Leonard
text: I don't get it. I already told her a lie. Why replace it with a different lie?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, first of all, your lie was laughably transparent, where mine is exquisitely convoluted. While you were sleeping, I was weaving an un-unravelable web.

speaker: Leonard
text: Un-unravelable?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes. If she googles Leopold Houston, she'll find a Facebook page, an online blog depicting his descent into drug use, and a desperate yet hopeful listing on eharmony.com.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay, why would I go to a drug intervention for your cousin?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Ah, because it's in Long Beach, and I don't drive.

speaker: Leonard
text: We're going to Long Beach?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, of course not. There's no cousin Leo. There's no intervention. Focus, Leonard.

speaker: Leonard
text: Oh, come on.

speaker: Sheldon
text: We just leave the house on Friday night, and we return in the wee hours, emotionally wrung out from the work of convincing Leo to go back into rehab.

speaker: Leonard
text: He goes back into rehab?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, but he can relapse if Penny ever invites us to hear her sing again.

speaker: Leonard
text: You still told her I lied.

speaker: Sheldon
text: For a noble purpose. To spare me the social embarrassment of having a drug-addled first cousin. Which I'm assuming is embarrassing, yes?

speaker: Leonard
text: How am I supposed to remember all of this?

speaker: Sheldon
text: That's the best part. You don't have to. See, I told Penny that you would be embarrassed if you knew that she found out that you had lied. So she's agreed to operate as if the original lie is still in force.
